history.summary: FLAG - THIS IS A JAIN (SHVETAMBARA) TIRTH, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed for a Hindu-temples dataset. The 'Jain Temple Triad' is the group of historic Jain derasars in the Chandi Bazaar / Shakar Tekri area near Bedi Gate, Jamnagar (address given as Summair Club Road, Shakar Tekri). Three temples were built between 1574 and 1622. The most intricate is Raisi Shah's temple, dedicated to the 16th Tirthankara Shantinath, whose sanctum dome is decorated with gold inlay work; its chambers feature elaborate geometric marble floors and mirrored ceilings. Next is the Vardhman Shah temple, dedicated to the 1st Tirthankara Adinath - a simpler structure but more vibrant in colour. A third, smaller temple completes the triad. A fourth marble temple (Sheth's Temple, Vasupujya Swami's Temple) is listed with the group in some accounts, and there are 30+ Jain temples in the city in total - the exact membership of 'the triad' is UNVERIFIED. The Shantinath Mandir has intricate carvings and wall murals depicting Jain saints.

name: Jain Temple Triad, Jamnagar
town_description: Jamnagar is a coastal city in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, on the Gulf of Kutch, founded in 1540 by Jam Rawal of the Jadeja Rajput clan as Nawanagar. Nicknamed 'Chhoti Kashi' (Little Kashi) for its many temples, it is a major pilgrim and tourist hub whose landmarks include Lakhota Lake, the Lakhota Palace museum and the Bala Hanuman temple. The city is also an industrial centre, home to one of the world's largest oil refining complexes at nearby Motikhavdi.
